verses.1: Why do the nations rage and the peoples conspire in vain?
verses.2: The kings of the earth have taken their stand, and the rulers have gathered together against the LORD and against His anointed.
verses.3: Let us tear their bonds apart and cast their ropes from us.
verses.4: The One who dwells in the heavens will laugh; the Lord will mock them.
verses.5: Then He will speak to them in His anger, and in His fury He will alarm them.
verses.6: But I have set My king on Mount Zion, My holy hill.
verses.7: I will declare the decree of the LORD: He said to Me, “You are My son; today I have begotten You.”
verses.8: Ask of Me, and I will give You the nations as Your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as Your possession.
verses.9: You will shepherd them with a rod of iron, as clay vessels You will shatter them.
verses.10: Now then, you kings, be wise; take warning, all you rulers of the earth.
verses.11: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
verses.12: Kiss the Son, lest He be angry and you perish from the way, when His anger flares suddenly. How blessed are all who take refuge in Him!

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "His anointed" is used for *mashiach*, following the glossary.
- v. 7: "I will declare the decree" is a rendering of *asapher*, which can mean "declare" or "proclaim."
- v. 9: "Rod of iron" and "as clay vessels" preserve the poetic imagery in the Hebrew without adding interpretive clarification.
